newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada March budget gap up, target to be bettered.
newsitem.headline: Canada March budget gap up, target to be bettered.

text.p: Canada's federal budget deficit rose to C$1.81 billion in March from C$1.18 billion a year earlier, the Finance Department said on Wednesday.

For the full fiscal year ended March, the deficit totalled C$9.64 billion, down sharply from C$24.46 billion in the same period a year earlier. But the figures to date are not the final results for fiscal 1996-97, since the Finance Department still needs to make regular end-of-year accounting adjustments. The adjustments incorporate increases to program spending to include the costs of liabilities during the fiscal year for which no payments were made in 1996-97, the department said.
But the department said the adjustments over the last three fiscal years have ranged from C$4 billion to C$6.5 billion.
"The results to the end of March 1997 suggest that the deficit for the year as a whole will be no higher than C$16 billion," the Finance Department said in its monthly Fiscal Monitor.
In Regina on Tuesday, Liberal Prime Minister Jean Chretien said the final figure might be even lower.
"He said it could be as low as C$15 billion or C$16 billion," Liberal spokesman Sean Kirby said in a phone interview.
The final results are expected in the fall.
Budgetary transactions (in billions of dollars)
Operating balance +1.99 +2.81 +35.11 +22.19
Public debt charges -3.80 -3.99 -44.75 -46.65
Fin source (excl forex) +0.16 -1.77 +1.13 -16.93
Forex transactions -2.06 -3.18 -7.52 -4.74
(Note: Positive numbers indicate net source of funds. Negative numbers indicate net requirement for funds.)

The department said the increase in the March 1997 budget deficit was largely due to higher personal income tax refunds, lower corporate income tax collections and the inclusion of the funding for the Canada Foundation for Innovation, announced in the February 1997 budget.
Offsetting these factors were unusually high goods and service tax collections, the department said.

For the year to date, budgetary revenues were up C$8.9 billion or 6.9 percent on a year-over-yhear basis, the department said. Over half of this improvement was due to special factors, such as higher personal income installment payments, the acceleration of employment insurance premium payments, the sale of the air navigation system and the timing of the collection of the goods and services tax.
Program spending was down C$4.0 billion or 3.8 percent, primarily reflecting the impact of the restraint measures introduced in the 1994 and 1995 budgets, the department said.
And public debt charges for the year to date were down by C$1.9 billion or 4.1 percent, reflecting a decline in interest rates, especially short-term rates.
The Finance Department said the financial source of C$1.1 billion reported in 1996-97 will be largely unaffected by the end-of-year accounting adjustments.
